title: Installing & Using Third‑Party Libraries 📦
description: Install external packages with pip and use requests and BeautifulSoup for web hacking.

slides.title: Beyond the Standard Library
slides.content:
# pip install Opens the Universe

Python's standard library is huge, but the real magic for hacking is in third‑party packages:
* **`requests`** – HTTP for humans (GET, POST, sessions, cookies)
* **`beautifulsoup4`** – HTML parsing
* **`scapy`** – packet manipulation
* **`paramiko`** – SSH
* **`cryptography`** – encryption

Install them with:
```
pip install requests beautifulsoup4
```

slides.title: Make an HTTP GET Request
slides.codeSnippet:
import requests
response = requests.get('http://httpbin.org/get')
print(response.status_code)
print(response.json())

quizData.question: What does `response.status_code` contain after a successful GET?
quizData.explanation: status_code is an integer like 200, 404, etc.

slides.title: requests with Parameters & Headers
slides.content:
# Customize Your Requests

```python
import requests
params = {'q': 'python hacking'}
headers = {'User-Agent': 'CybronScanner/1.0'}
resp = requests.get('https://api.github.com/search/repositories',
                     params=params, headers=headers)
print(resp.url)   # see full URL with query string
```
This is how you interact with web APIs.

slides.title: POST Request Example
slides.codeSnippet:
import requests
login_url = 'http://httpbin.org/post'
data = {'username': 'admin', 'password': 'secret'}
resp = requests.post(login_url, data=data)
print(resp.json())

quizData.question: `requests.get` and `requests.post` are the only HTTP methods available in the requests library.
quizData.explanation: requests also supports put, patch, delete, head, options.

slides.title: BeautifulSoup – Parse HTML 🍲
slides.content:
# Extract Data from Web Pages

```python
from bs4 import BeautifulSoup
import requests

url = 'http://example.com'
resp = requests.get(url)
soup = BeautifulSoup(resp.text, 'html.parser')
print(soup.title.string)  # page title
links = soup.find_all('a')
for link in links:
    print(link.get('href'))
```
BeautifulSoup transforms messy HTML into a searchable tree.

slides.title: Extract All Links
slides.codeSnippet: from bs4 import BeautifulSoup html = 'Link1Link2' soup = BeautifulSoup(html, 'html.parser') for a_tag in soup.find_all('a'): print(a_tag['href'])

quizData.question: How do you select the first `<h1>` tag in a soup object?
quizData.explanation: soup.h1 returns the first h1 tag; find_all returns a list.

slides.title: Installing Packages in a Virtual Environment
slides.content:
# Remember Chapter 2?

Always create a virtual environment before installing third‑party packages:
```bash
python3 -m venv webscan
source webscan/bin/activate
pip install requests beautifulsoup4
```
This keeps your global Python clean and your project reproducible.

slides.title: Pro Tip 💡
slides.content:
## Check package documentation

Most packages have great docs online. For requests: docs.python-requests.org. For BeautifulSoup: crummy.com/software/BeautifulSoup/bs4/doc/.
